title: Right to Remain Silent (Article 20(3))
content:
Under Article 20(3) of the Constitution of India, no person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against themselves. This means:

• You have the right to remain silent during police questioning.
• Police cannot force you to confess or make statements.
• Silence cannot be held against you in court.
• You have the right to consult a lawyer before answering any questions.

**What to do:**
- When detained, immediately ask for a lawyer.
- Do not sign any documents without your lawyer present.
- You may say: "I wish to remain silent and will speak only in the presence of my lawyer."

title: Right to Inform Family / Friend (BNSS Section 36)
content:
Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023, Section 36, every arrested person has the right to have a nominated person informed of their arrest.

• Police must inform you of this right immediately upon arrest.
• You have the right to make a phone call to inform someone.
• This right exists regardless of the alleged offence.

**What to do:**
- Immediately ask to make a phone call.
- Memorize at least one emergency contact number.
- If police refuse, note their names and badge numbers.

title: Produced Before Magistrate Within 24 Hours (Article 22(2), BNSS Section 176)
content:
Article 22(2) of the Constitution and BNSS Section 176 mandate that an arrested person must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (excluding travel time).

• This prevents illegal detention.
• The magistrate reviews whether the arrest is lawful.
• If the 24-hour limit is violated, the detention becomes illegal.

**What to do:**
- Keep track of the time of your arrest.
- Inform your lawyer if not produced within 24 hours.
- File a habeas corpus petition if illegally detained.

title: Rights During Search & Seizure (BNSS Sections 104-105)
content:
BNSS Sections 104-105 provide protections during searches:

• Police must conduct searches in the presence of two independent witnesses (panchas).
• You have the right to be present during the search of your premises.
• A search warrant must be shown before entering your premises (with limited exceptions).
• You have the right to receive a copy of the search list/inventory.
• Women cannot be searched by male officers — only by female officers.
• Searches may be video recorded as a safeguard.

**What to do:**
- Ask to see the search warrant.
- Record the search on your phone if possible.
- Note names of the police officers and panch witnesses.
- Demand a copy of the search inventory.

title: Right to Free Legal Aid (Article 39A, BNSS Section 386)
content:
Article 39A of the Constitution guarantees free legal aid. BNSS Section 386 provides legal aid at state expense:

• If you cannot afford a lawyer, the state must provide one free of cost.
• This right applies from the moment of arrest.
• The magistrate must inform you of this right at first production.
• Legal aid lawyers available at all district courts.

**What to do:**
- State clearly: "I cannot afford a lawyer. I request free legal aid."
- Contact District Legal Services Authority (DLSA).
- NALSA helpline: 15100

title: No Torture or Cruel Treatment (Article 21, BNS Section 330)
content:
Article 21 of the Constitution guarantees the right against torture. BNS Section 330 (replacing IPC) makes it a crime to cause hurt to extort confession:

• Police cannot use physical force, threats, or intimidation.
• Confessions under duress are not admissible as evidence.
• You have the right to medical examination immediately upon arrest.

**What to do:**
- If tortured, demand immediate medical examination.
- File complaint with magistrate or NHRC (helpline: 14440).
- Preserve evidence of injuries (photos, medical reports).

title: Right to Bail for Bailable Offences (BNSS Section 478)
content:
BNSS Section 478 provides that a person arrested for a bailable offence has the right to be released on bail:

• Bail is a right, not a favour, for bailable offences.
• Police cannot keep you in custody if you provide bail.
• For non-bailable offences, bail is at court discretion.

**What to do:**
- Ask what section you are being arrested under.
- Check if the offence is bailable.
- Arrange for bail as quickly as possible.

title: Rights of Women During Arrest (BNSS Section 47)
content:
BNSS Section 47 provides special protections for women during arrest:

• A woman cannot be arrested before sunrise or after sunset without magistrate permission.
• Only a female police officer can arrest a woman.
• Female arrestees must be searched only by female officers.
• Women have the right to be kept in separate lock-ups.

**What to do:**
- Assert these rights if violated.
- Note time if arrested at night illegally.
- Contact women's helpline: 181 or 1091.
